findings.text: Deferred work uses a tiny cancellation token holding one boolean flag. The token is passed by value to handlers so each handler can observe cancellation without dereferencing shared request state.

Request flag bit numbers zero through six mirror submission options for fixed file, drain, link, hard link, forced async, buffer select and completion skip. Internal tracking starts at position 8 and uses successive positions, with a terminal sentinel that lets the build verify the set still fits a 64 bit word.

Request flags form functional groups. Linkage covers drain, soft versus hard linkage, timeout arming and suppression of link completions on failure. Buffer handling covers selection, ring origin, commit duty, node validity, incremental consumption and import. Polling covers prior poll, single versus double registration, lazy wake opt out, pollability and multishot modes. Lifetime covers inflight membership, cleanup duty, reference counting, credential and async data presence, position use, reissue and polled completion duty.

The flag word uses a dedicated 64 bit bitwise type rather than a plain integer. Each named flag is formed by shifting one bit into that type, giving type checking against accidental arithmetic mixing while keeping one bit per property.

The internal completion entry carries a 64 bit user identifier and a signed 32 bit result. A trailing 32 bit slot is shared between completion flags and a descriptor value, with descriptor meaning during setup and flag meaning at completion.

Task work chaining combines an intrusive singly linked node with a callback pointer. The callback receives a small wrapper holding the target request plus the cancellation token, allowing deferred execution without extra allocation.

Pass through commands share a container starting with a file pointer followed by 56 payload bytes. A compile time size guard rejects any command extension larger than that container, so opcode data must fit the fixed budget.

The io_kiocb descriptor overlays a bare file pointer with the command container, relying on the file pointer being first in every overlay member so either view yields the same address. It then stores a one byte opcode, a one byte polled marker, a two byte buffer index, the flag word, an embedded completion, ring and task context pointers, and a conditional buffer pointer selecting between a chosen buffer and a resource node.

The tail of io_kiocb multiplexes uses through unions. Completion batching shares space with cached poll events, deferred work shares space with a hybrid poll timestamp, and a hash node shares space with a poll list node and a reclaim head. Remaining members hold a file node, reference counts, a cancellation marker, async poll and async data pointers, a link pointer, optional credentials, a work item, two extra completion words, and a separate overflow element linking a full completion for later delivery.

Several io_kiocb fields are valid only with companion flags. The selected buffer pointer needs buffer selected, the node alternative covers ring sourced buffers, credentials need creds present, the link pointer needs link or hard link mode, async data needs async data allocated, and the buffer index means either fixed index or selected identifier depending on buffer mode.

Per queue io_cq state pairs queue and owning context pointers with a flag word and two unions that reuse list linkage for reclaim caching and deferred freeing after exit. The io_context owner holds a long reference count, an active count and a priority, plus optionally a spinlock, a radix tree, a hint pointer, a hash list and a release work item.

When queue tracking is configured, one spinlock inside io_context serializes its tree, hint and list of queue states. Callers must hold it to insert, look up or remove queue state, and the hint and list are unstable without it.
Queue state exit marker uses numeric value 4 and destroy marker uses value 8, occupying distinct bits that may combine in the flag word.

Process I/O context copying has two builds. One checks whether current task owns context and either succeeds at once when none exists or delegates to a shared helper. The disabled build always succeeds without touching task state, and companion put and exit helpers become silent no operation stubs there.

Unmapped page checking has an active build that consults a static branch gate and calls the shared checker only when debugging is enabled, and a disabled build where the same page plus length call performs no action.

DMA IOMMU use has an enabled build forwarding the device to a capability query and a disabled build always reporting false. Noncontiguous unmapping is defined as unmapping the supplied virtual address directly.

Three helpers describe mapping arithmetic. One caps a transfer by a DMA mask after accounting for offset. A second reports whether an element crosses a power of two boundary from index, count, shift and boundary size. A third rounds address plus length up to whole I/O pages for a given page size.
Mapping protections use value 1 for read, 2 for write, 4 for cache coherence, 8 for no execute, 16 for MMIO style use and 32 for privileged. Each is one bit so combinations add.

Fault permissions use 1 for read, 2 for write, 4 for execute and 8 for privileged. The page request fault type uses value 1. Page request options use 1 for PASID valid, 2 for last page and 4 for response needs PASID. Legacy direction uses 0 for read and 1 for write, and dirty no clear uses value 1.

A fault pairs a 32 bit type with a page request payload holding flags, PASID, group identifier, permission bits, faulting address and two private words. A page response carries PASID, group and a code where 0 means success, 1 invalid and 2 failure.

Recoverable fault handling wraps each fault with list linkage. A group keeps the terminating fault inline plus a list and count of related faults, a pending node, a work item, an attach handle, device fault state, a provider hook node and a cookie. A queue holds a workqueue, a device list and a mutex.
The fault queue colocates a mutex with its device list and workqueue, indicating the mutex guards device membership. The fragments do not show further ordering against group lists or work dispatch.

Domain capability bits use 1 for paging, 2 for DMA API, 4 for identity, 8 for flush queue, 16 for shared address, 32 for platform and 64 for nested. Named composites combine them for blocked, identity, unmanaged, DMA, DMA with flush queue, shared, platform and nested uses, and the allocation mask allows all bits except flush queue.

Domain geometry stores an inclusive mappable interval plus a flag mandating DMA stay inside. Cookie roles enumerate none, IOVA, MSI, fault handler, shared address and IOMMUFD. The domain stores type, cookie role, page table marker, operation pointers, owner, page size bitmap, geometry, group handler and a cookie union whose active member follows the role. A predicate reports DMA API membership by testing the DMA bit, and capability codes cover coherence, no execute, pre boot protection, enforce coherence, deferred flush, dirty tracking and PCI ATS.

Reservation regions link into lists and store start, length, protection, a type selecting direct, relaxable direct, reserved, hardware MSI or software MSI, plus a device specific free callback. RMR data extends a region with stream identifiers and a count. PASID reserves 0 for DMA without PASID, starts global allocation at 1 and uses all bits set for invalid, with a dedicated unsigned identifier type.

Page freeing uses a list wrapper with an initializer for an empty list. IOTLB gathering records an inclusive interval, either a flush interval or bitmaps of cleared leaf and table levels, a freelist and a queued flag for full flush. Dirty tracking pairs a bitmap with its gather, and dirty operations offer enablement plus read and clear over domain, address, size, flags and bitmap holder.
User IOMMU parameters use a type tag, user pointer and length, with an array variant adding per entry length and entry count so variable arrays can be validated without trusting user length alone.

User struct copying first validates descriptors, requires matching type tags and enforces minimum and maximum lengths before delegating to a generic copier. That copier copies the shared prefix, zero fills a short user buffer, rejects a long user buffer unless trailing bytes are all zero, checks kernel size against known object size, and reports faults or oversize with distinct errors.

Helpers fail closed on bad input. Null descriptors, mismatched types and bad lengths are rejected, oversized kernel targets take a warning path, nonzero trailing bytes are rejected, user copy faults are reported, non power of two boundaries abort, oversized command payloads fail at build time, and flag overflow is caught by a terminal bit.

A request moves from linkage through buffer preparation, poll registration and completion. Link mode chains successors with failure propagation unless hard linked, inflight marks cancellable membership, selection advances to commit for ring buffers, poll passes single or double registration with optional multishot rearm, and terminal paths select reissue, async punt, polled completion or overflow queueing.

Recoverable faults accumulate into a group that grows its list and count until the terminating fault arrives, then waits on a pending queue and is driven by its work item toward a handler using cookie and device state. The fragments show lists, count, pending node and work linkage but not handler outcomes.
